title: Boundaries (GeoJSON)
text:
The dataset’s curated output is the per-class (hierarchical) GeoJSON collection — e.g. barangays, provinces, municipalities, and cities split by legal class (highly urbanized, independent component, component). Every polygon is enriched with its canonical PSGC code, name, and status. Boundaries originate from NAMRIA shapefiles (v2023-11-06); PSGC codes from PSA snapshots (latest: 2023-10-24).
The full adm0–adm4 enriched files and the pre-enrichment raw NAMRIA conversion are also available as intermediate transformation stages of the pipeline that produces the hierarchical output.

title: Boundaries (GeoJSON)
text:
Data transformation tiers
The pipeline runs in three tiers — raw (NAMRIA shapefile → GeoJSON, no PSGC) → enriched (adds psgc_code/name/status) → hierarchical (per-class extracts, the curated end product). See Pipeline B for the full transformation, and Releases & versioning for the v<YYYY-MM-DD> tag convention.
Every file is available two ways: as a versioned GitHub Release asset (pinned to a v<YYYY-MM-DD> tag, with manifest.json checksums) or in-repo at 2023-10-24/{tier}_t0p005/ via raw.githubusercontent.com.

title: Philippine Boundaries & PSGC
text: Curated hierarchical Philippine administrative boundaries as GeoJSON — barangays, municipalities, and cities split by legal class (highly urbanized, independent component, component), plus provinces, regions, and special geographic areas — each polygon annotated with its canonical PSGC code, name, and status. Generated from PSA Philippine Standard Geographic Code snapshots and NAMRIA administrative-boundary shapefiles, with the full quarterly change history published as W3C ORG RDF linked data. The enriched (adm0–adm4) and raw NAMRIA-converted files are kept as intermediate pipeline stages.

title: Philippine Boundaries & PSGC
text:
Pick your path
This dataset ships two data products plus a full developer toolchain. Choose the section that matches what you need.



Boundaries (GeoJSON) ›
Curated per-class Philippine boundary polygons (barangays, municipalities, cities by class, provinces, regions, special geographic areas), each tagged with its PSGC code. For data consumers — the 95% case.


Change history (RDF) ›
The quarterly PSGC change history as W3C ORG linked data — creation, merger, split, transfer, rename, code-change events across 17 snapshots. For linked-data / semantic users.


Toolchain ›
The brgybnd CLI, the two pipelines (PSGC → RDF and NAMRIA → GeoJSON), data model, configuration, and repository layout. For developers and reproducers.



Cross-cutting reference material (PSGC codes, HUC mapping, citation) lives under References; dataset/version history lives in the Changelog and the per-snapshot timeline under Change history (RDF).

text:
Cross-cutting look-up material that applies across the Boundaries, Change history (RDF), and Toolchain sections.

HUC mapping — the Highly Urbanized City / Metro Manila mismatch and how it is resolved.
Citation — how to cite this dataset.

title: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch
text: A Highly Urbanized City (HUC) is a Philippine city that is administratively independent of any province and reports directly to the region. Examples: Quezon City, Makati, Davao City, Cebu City.
crumbs: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch

crumbs: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch

title: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch
text:
The mismatch






Warning



Two authoritative sources disagree about an HUC’s parent:







Source
HUC parent recorded as




PSGC (PSA)
the region


NAMRIA boundaries
the province it sits geographically inside



A naive parent-lookup that joins NAMRIA polygons to PSGC by province would therefore misclassify every HUC (e.g. place Makati under Rizal Province instead of NCR).
crumbs: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch

title: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch
text:
How this dataset resolves it
The script generate_huc_mapping.py produces namria/huc_adm2_mapping.json, an explicit lookup from each HUC to its correct PSGC parent. This mapping is consumed by:

coverage.py — so coverage stats count HUCs correctly.
enrich.py — so each HUC feature gets the right psgc_code and parent.
crumbs: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch

title: HUC mapping — Highly Urbanized Cities and the NAMRIA province mismatch

Metro Manila: virtual provinces
Metro Manila (NCR) has no PSGC province-level units — it is regions → cities → barangays directly. NAMRIA, however, publishes the four NCR legislative districts as ADM2 polygons. To reconcile, this dataset maps those districts as virtual provinces of type mm_district:

Mapped type




Metropolitan Manila First District

Metropolitan Manila Second District

Metropolitan Manila Third District
mm_district (virtual province)


Metropolitan Manila Fourth District
mm_district (virtual province)



These four features appear in non_administrative.geojson because they are not standard PSGC provinces — they are documented honestly rather than silently dropped.

Because HUCs require special handling, enriched features carry a match_confidence value (exact / huc_map / fuzzy) — see feature properties.
For the 2023-10-24 snapshot, 31 of 34 HUCs matched exactly, 1 via the HUC map, and 2 via fuzzy matching.

title: Change history (RDF)
text: This dataset publishes two data products. The Boundaries (GeoJSON) section covers the spatial polygons; this section covers the linked-data change history — the output of Pipeline A.

title: Change history (RDF)
text:
What the RDF is
For every PSGC snapshot, Pipeline A emits a delta (delta.ttl / delta.nt / delta.jsonld) describing how Philippine administrative units changed relative to the previous snapshot: created, deleted, renamed, merged, split, transferred, reclassified, or re-coded. The deltas are serialized on the W3C ORG ontology with PROV provenance and Dublin Core terms.

title: Change history (RDF)
text:
Why it exists
PSGC codes are not stable: barangays are continually created, merged, split, renamed, transferred between parents, and re-coded. The RDF deltas let a downstream system track an entity’s identity across quarters via the 9-digit correspondence code (see PSGC code structure) and answer questions like “what happened to barangay X between 2023 and 2024?”.

title: Change history (RDF)
PSGC snapshot history
text: This dataset tracks 17 quarterly PSGC snapshots. Each snapshot is processed into an RDF delta (delta.ttl / .nt / .jsonld) capturing creation, deletion, transfer, merger, split, renaming, reclassification, and code-change events relative to the previous snapshot — see change-event types.

title: PSGC snapshot history
text:
Reading the deltas
Each snapshot directory in the repository contains delta.ttl (Turtle), delta.nt (N-Triples), and delta.jsonld (JSON-LD), plus the source PSA press release as Markdown. The RDF uses the W3C ORG ontology with PROV provenance and Dublin Core terms.
For dataset and documentation versions (release tags), see the Changelog; for the version-tag convention see Releases & versioning.

title: Ontology & namespaces
text: The PSGC change-history RDF is built on the W3C ORG ontology for organizational structure, with PROV for provenance, Dublin Core Terms for metadata, and per-snapshot PSGC concepts.

title: Ontology & namespaces
text:
Namespaces
Namespaces used across the delta files:

org: — W3C ORG (FormalOrganization for Reg/Prov/City/Mun, OrganizationalUnit for Bgy/SubMun)
psgc: — the project’s own vocabulary (entity / event / concept URIs — see URIs)
dct: — Dublin Core Terms (title, source, legal basis metadata)
prov: — PROV-O provenance (linking events to their snapshot and source PSA press release)
time: — temporal positioning of effective / plebiscite dates
schema: — schema.org supplementary terms

title: Ontology & namespaces
text:
Ontology mapping

PSGC level → ORG class
Each PSGC level is typed as one of two ORG classes (from rdf/builder.py):








PSGC level
ORG class
Typed as




Region (Reg)
org:FormalOrganization
autonomous top-level unit


Province (Prov)
org:FormalOrganization



Municipality (Mun)
org:FormalOrganization



City (City)
org:FormalOrganization



Barangay (Bgy)
org:OrganizationalUnit
sub-unit


Sub-municipality (SubMun)
org:OrganizationalUnit
sub-unit




A delta only emits the entities touched by that quarter’s changes, so a delta may contain only OrganizationalUnit instances (e.g. the 2023-10-24 delta is all barangays). The --full build emits the entire entity graph with both classes.



Hierarchy
Parent/child relationships are derived from the PSGC code structure and encoded with ORG containment predicates in full builds:

org:hasSubOrganization — FormalOrganization → FormalOrganization (e.g. region → province, province → city/municipality).
org:hasUnit — FormalOrganization → OrganizationalUnit (e.g. municipality → barangay).



Change events
Each change is an org:ChangeEvent typed via org:classification → a psgc:concept/change-type/{type} concept. The participating entities are attached with org:originalOrganization (the pre-change entity) and org:resultingOrganization (the post-change entity). See Change-event types for the per-type triple shape.


Provenance & metadata
Each change event carries its provenance: dct:source for the legal basis (Republic Act number, Executive Order, plebiscite resolution, etc.), prov:generatedAtTime for the effective date, and dct:description for a human-readable summary of what changed and why.

title: Serialisations
text: Every snapshot directory ships the same delta in three RDF serialisations.

title: Serialisations
text:
Formats








File
Format
When to use




delta.ttl
Turtle
Human-readable, compact; default for browsing/editing


delta.nt
N-Triples
Streaming / line-oriented ingestion; no prefix declarations


delta.jsonld
JSON-LD
Web/JS consumers; embeddable in JSON pipelines; links to schema.org context

title: Serialisations
Serialisations
text:
Consistency across snapshots
The three serialisations are generated from the same in-memory graph. Treat the Turtle file as canonical when the three disagree.

title: Toolchain
text: The brgybnd CLI converts PSA PSGC Excel/PDF snapshots into RDF linked data (W3C ORG ontology) and matches NAMRIA shapefile boundaries with PSGC codes to produce hierarchical per-class GeoJSON — the curated end product — plus enriched and raw stages as intermediate pipeline outputs.

title: Toolchain
text:
Tech stack
Python 3.13 · Hatchling build · UV package manager · Click CLI · Pydantic v2 · rdflib · geopandas · OpenAI-compatible LLM client.

title: Toolchain
text:
Two parallel pipelines
The repository runs two independent pipelines side by side:

Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF. Parses PSGC Excel/PDF snapshots, normalizes ~50 raw change types to 10 canonical ones, builds an ORG-ontology RDF graph, and computes per-snapshot deltas. See Pipeline A: PSGC → RDF.
Pipeline B — NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON. Converts NAMRIA shapefiles to GeoJSON, enriches every polygon with its PSGC code (handling the HUC mismatch), classifies features by PSGC type/class, and splits into per-class files. See Pipeline B: NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON.

title: Toolchain
text:
Data tiers
Pipeline B produces three tiers: raw (NAMRIA-converted, pre-enrichment) → enriched (adm0–adm4 annotated with psgc_code/name/status/match_confidence) → hierarchical (the curated per-class end product that GitHub Releases publish). See Pipeline B and the Boundaries overview.

title: Toolchain
text:
Install
The project is managed with UV and targets Python 3.13. From a clone of the repository:
# install dependencies into the project environment
uv sync

# expose the brgybnd CLI globally (optional)
uv tool install .
This installs the brgybnd entry point (barangay_boundaries_repository/cli:cli) — see the CLI reference for the 10 subcommands.

Required inputs
brgybnd reads from two on-disk sources that are not committed to this repo (too large):

PSGC snapshots — live under $PSGC_DATA_DIR (default ~/commons/barangay), in per-snapshot YYYY-MM-DD/ subdirectories of Excel/PDF files that ingest/scanner.py classifies. Set this in configuration or via the PSGC_DATA_DIR environment variable.
NAMRIA shapefiles — committed under namria/ (phl_admbnda_adm{0-4}_*.shp, version 2023-11-06).

The optional LLM batch-extraction step of Pipeline A needs OPENAI_API_KEY (defaults target the GLM API). Everything else runs offline. See configuration.
For a copy-paste quick start (install + first run), see the README.

title: Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF
text: Pipeline A turns PSA PSGC Excel/PDF snapshots into W3C ORG RDF linked data, and computes a per-snapshot change-history delta. Its end product is the delta.{ttl,nt,jsonld} files that live under each YYYY-MM-DD/ snapshot directory — see the Change history (RDF) section for consuming them.

title: Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF
text:
Flow





flowchart LR
  src["PSGC XLSX snapshots<br/>(~/commons/barangay/YYYY-MM-DD/)"]
  scanner["ingest/scanner.py<br/>classify files by regex"]
  xlsx["ingest/xlsx_parser.py<br/>PSGC sheet + changes; ~50 → 10 canonical change types"]
  pdf["ingest/pdf_parser.py<br/>OCR text from press-release PDFs"]
  agent["agent/pipeline.py<br/>(optional) LLM batch extraction"]
  builder["rdf/builder.py<br/>ORG ontology graph"]
  delta["rdf/delta.py<br/>compute_delta()"]
  out[("YYYY-MM-DD/<br/>delta.{ttl,nt,jsonld}")]

  src --> scanner --> xlsx --> pdf
  pdf -.optional.-> agent --> builder
  xlsx --> builder
  builder --> delta --> out

title: Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF
text:
Stages

ingest/scanner.py — classifies snapshot files by regex (datafile, changes, press release, province summary).
ingest/xlsx_parser.py — parses the PSGC sheet (entities) + changes sheets; normalizes ~50 raw change types to 10 canonical ones.
ingest/pdf_parser.py — OCR text from PDF press releases (kreuzberg).
agent/pipeline.py (optional) — LLM batch extraction (structured JSON output, batches of 50 entities / 100 changes). See configuration for the required env vars.
rdf/builder.py — builds the RDF graph on the ORG ontology.
rdf/delta.py — compute_delta() between two snapshots.

title: Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF
text:
Detected change-event types
compute_delta() detects: creation, deletion, code_change, rename, merger, split, name_correction, transfer. See RDF event types and the PSGC code structure reference (9-digit correspondence codes drive identity tracking across code changes).

title: Pipeline A — PSGC → RDF
text:
Running it
brgybnd ingest --date 2023-10-24
brgybnd process --date 2023-10-24 --format turtle
See the CLI reference for all flags.

title: Configuration
text:
.env example
A .env in the repository root (loaded by config.py via python-dotenv) only needs the data directory in practice; the three OPENAI_* vars are for the optional Pipeline A LLM step and can be omitted for offline runs:
# required to point at the PSGC snapshot source tree
PSGC_DATA_DIR=~/commons/barangay

# optional — only for the LLM batch-extraction step of Pipeline A
OPENAI_API_KEY=your-key
OPENAI_BASE_URL=https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4/
OPENAI_MODEL=glm-4.7
PSGC_DATA_DIR is the root of the snapshot tree. ingest/scanner.py expects each snapshot as a per-quarter subdirectory named YYYY-MM-DD/ (e.g. 2023-10-24/) containing the PSA Excel datafile, the changes sheet(s), and the PDF press release — it classifies the files inside by filename regex. Pointing PSGC_DATA_DIR anywhere else just relocates that tree.
The GLM defaults (OPENAI_BASE_URL / OPENAI_MODEL) target the Z.ai GLM endpoint; set them to any OpenAI-compatible base URL and structured-output model of your choice.

title: Pipeline B — NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON
text: Pipeline B turns NAMRIA administrative-boundary shapefiles into the curated hierarchical per-class GeoJSON that is the dataset’s recommended end product. Its intermediate stages — raw and enriched — are documented under Boundaries.

title: Pipeline B — NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON
text:
Flow





flowchart LR
  shp[("namria/phl_admbnda_adm{0-4}_*.shp<br/>v2023-11-06")]
  conv["namria_converter.py<br/>shapefile → GeoJSON<br/>(Douglas-Peucker simplify, 0.005°)"]
  raw[("stage 1:<br/>raw_t0p005/")]
  cov["coverage.py<br/>PSGC pcode vs GeoJSON pcode"]
  huc["generate_huc_mapping.py<br/>huc_adm2_mapping.json<br/>(HUCs, MM districts, SGAs)"]
  enrich["enrich.py<br/>adds psgc_id / code / name / status / match_confidence"]
  enr[("stage 2:<br/>enriched_t0p005/")]
  cls["classifier.py<br/>assigns PSGC type/class"]
  split["splitter.py<br/>per-class files"]
  hier["hierarchical.py<br/>orchestrate classify → split → report"]
  cur[("curated:<br/>hierarchical_t0p005/<br/><class>.geojson +<br/>classification_report.json +<br/>summary.md")]

  shp --> conv --> raw
  raw --> cov --> huc --> enrich --> enr
  enr --> cls --> split --> hier --> cur

title: Pipeline B — NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON
text:
Stages

namria_converter.py — shapefile → GeoJSON (Douglas-Peucker simplify, default 0.005°). Output: raw tier.
coverage.py — PSGC pcode vs GeoJSON pcode comparison per admin level.
generate_huc_mapping.py — builds huc_adm2_mapping.json for HUCs, MM districts, and Special Geographic Areas. See HUC mapping generation and the HUC mapping reference.
enrich.py — adds psgc_id, psgc_code, psgc_name, psgc_status, match_confidence. Output: enriched tier.
classifier.py — assigns the PSGC type/class (barangay, HUC, ICC, component city, …) per feature.
splitter.py — splits enriched features into per-class files.
hierarchical.py — orchestrates phases 3–5 (classify → split → report). Output: the curated hierarchical tier plus classification_report.json and summary.md.

title: Pipeline B — NAMRIA → hierarchical GeoJSON
text:
Running it
brgybnd build-hierarchical --date 2023-10-24
build-hierarchical runs convert → enrich → classify → split. Use --skip-convert / --skip-enrich to reuse existing intermediate stages. See the CLI reference.

title: HUC mapping generation
text: generate_huc_mapping.py is a standalone script that produces namria/huc_adm2_mapping.json, the explicit lookup consumed by coverage.py and enrich.py in Pipeline B.

title: HUC mapping generation
text:
The problem
Highly Urbanized Cities have PSGC parent = region (not province), but NAMRIA places them under provinces. Metro Manila also lacks PSGC province-level units — NAMRIA’s 4 NCR legislative districts are mapped as virtual_provinces of type mm_district.
See the HUC mapping reference for the full domain explanation and the consumer-facing impact.

title: HUC mapping generation
text:
Consumers
The generated huc_adm2_mapping.json is consumed by:

coverage.py — so coverage stats count HUCs correctly.
enrich.py — so each HUC feature gets the right psgc_code and parent.

title: HUC mapping generation
text:
huc_adm2_mapping.json schema
The file (committed to each snapshot’s raw_t0p005/) is keyed by NAMRIA pcode and carries seven sections:







Section
Purpose




virtual_provinces
ADM2 pcodes that are not real provinces: HUCs (e.g. Isabela, type: huc_isabela), the four Metro Manila legislative districts (type: mm_district), and the SGA cluster (type: sga). Each maps to {psgc_code, psgc_pcode, name, type}.


metro_manila_districts
each NCR legislative-district pcode → the list of city pcodes it contains.


huc_cities_under_province
for each province pcode, the HUC cities NAMRIA nests under it (with their namria_adm3_pcode).


namria_adm3_to_psgc
direct ADM3 pcode → PSGC code lookup.


barmm_adm3_to_psgc
BARMM-specific ADM3 → PSGC lookup (post-2023 SGA reorganization).


submunicipality_parents
Manila sub-municipality parent pcodes.


cross_parent_mapping
cases where a feature’s parent differs between the two sources.

title: HUC mapping generation
text:
Regenerating
generate_huc_mapping.py is a standalone script — re-run it whenever the NAMRIA shapefiles or PSGC snapshot change:
python barangay_boundaries_repository/generate_huc_mapping.py
The output is written to namria/huc_adm2_mapping.json and copied into the snapshot’s raw_t0p005/ during the convert stage of Pipeline B.

title: HUC mapping generation
text:
Name sanitization
Matching NAMRIA names to PSGC names requires normalization — stripping "(Capital)" / "(Pob.)" suffixes, the "City of" prefix, diacritics, and punctuation. That step is duplicated in two places: generate_huc_mapping.py (≈ lines 180–193) and enrich.py (≈ lines 35–42). If you adjust the normalization rules, update both so the mapping file and the enrichment pass stay consistent (see AGENTS.md).

title: Querying the PSGC RDF

title: Querying the PSGC RDF
text:
Loading with rdflib
from rdflib import Graph

g = Graph()
g.parse("2023-10-24/delta.ttl", format="turtle")
print(len(g), "triples loaded")
Load several snapshots into one graph to query across time:
import glob
g = Graph()
for ttl in glob.glob("20*/delta.ttl"):
    g.parse(ttl, format="turtle")

title: Querying the PSGC RDF
Entity & event URIs
text: The RDF graph uses three URI patterns under the psgc: namespace.

title: Entity & event URIs
text:
URI patterns
psgc:entity/{code}              — entity URI
psgc:event/{date}/{seq}         — change event URI (seq = 0001, 0002, ...)
psgc:concept/{scheme}/{value}   — concept URI (for levels, classes, etc.)

psgc:entity/{code} — one per Philippine administrative unit, keyed by its 10-digit PSGC code (see PSGC code structure). Identity across code changes is tracked by the 9-digit correspondence code, not by this URI.
psgc:event/{date}/{seq} — one per detected change in a snapshot’s delta; the {seq} suffix (0001, 0002, …) disambiguates multiple events on the same date.
psgc:concept/{scheme}/{value} — concept URIs for levels (region/province/…/barangay), city classes (HUC/ICC/component), and other controlled vocabularies.

title: Entity & event URIs
Change-event types
text: compute_delta() (in rdf/delta.py) classifies the difference between two PSGC snapshots into a fixed set of canonical event types, emitted as psgc:event/... URIs (see URIs).

title: Change-event types
text:
Canonical event types
The authoritative set is the ChangeEvent.event_type enum in models/schemas.py (10 types). compute_delta() actually emits these seven:

creation — a new entity appears in the later snapshot.
deletion — an entity disappears.
code_change — identity preserved (same correspondence code), but the 10-digit PSGC code changed.
renaming — name change, same identity.
merger — two or more entities combine into one.
split — one entity divides into two or more.
transfer — an entity moves to a different parent unit.

The remaining three enum values — reclassification, reenlistment, and unknown — are modelled by the schema and accepted by the parser/RDF builder, but are not currently produced by compute_delta() (reclassifications, for example, surface as a creation+deletion pair today).

title: Change-event types
text:
Per-type triple shape
Every event is an org:ChangeEvent with a dct:date (the snapshot date), a dct:description, and an org:classification link to a psgc:concept/change-type/{type} concept. The difference between types is which organization links they carry:









Type
org:originalOrganization
org:resultingOrganization
Meaning




creation
—
✓ (1)
new entity appears


deletion
✓ (1)
—
entity disappears


code_change
✓ (1)
✓ (1)
same identity, new 10-digit PSGC code


renaming
✓ (1)
✓ (1)
name change, identity preserved


merger
✓ (n)
✓ (1)
several entities combine into one


split
✓ (1)
✓ (n)
one entity divides into several


transfer
✓ (1)
✓ (1)
entity moves to a different parent



Worked examples of these links are in Entity & event URIs.
Each committed delta carries the legal basis for its events via dct:source, the effective date via prov:generatedAtTime, and a human-readable summary via dct:description.

title: PSGC code structure
text: The Philippine Standard Geographic Code (PSGC) is a 10-digit hierarchical identifier maintained by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA). Each administrative unit occupies a fixed segment of the code.

title: PSGC code structure
text:
The 10-digit hierarchy
Format: PPCCCMMLLL0 (the final digit is a check/reserved position).










Segment
Digits
Level
Example code
Example




Region
PP
ADM1
1300000000
National Capital Region (NCR)


Province
PPCCC
ADM2
0139000000
(province segment)


Municipality/City
PPCCCMMLL
ADM3
1376020000
a municipality/city


Barangay
PPCCCMMLLL
ADM4
1376020068
a barangay




Worked example
1339060014 decodes as:

13 — NCR (region)
1339 — City of Makati (province-level / HUC)
133906 — City of Makati (municipality/city level)
1339060014 — a specific barangay within Makati

title: PSGC code structure
text:
Correspondence codes (9-digit identity)
A 9-digit correspondence code tracks an entity’s identity across PSGC code changes. When a barangay is renamed, merged, split, or transferred, its 10-digit PSGC code may change but its 9-digit correspondence code stays stable. This repository uses correspondence codes to compute deltas between snapshots.

title: PSGC code structure
text:
Code-change events detected
The RDF deltas (delta.{ttl,nt,jsonld}) classify changes into the canonical event types of the ChangeEvent.event_type enum — creation, deletion, transfer, renaming, merger, split, code_change, plus the model-only reclassification, reenlistment, and unknown. See change-event types for which of these compute_delta() actually emits.
See PSGC snapshot history for the 17 processed quarters.

title: Feature properties & schema
text: Every GeoJSON feature in the curated hierarchical per-class files carries a set of PSGC enrichment properties alongside the original NAMRIA source attributes.

title: Feature properties & schema
text:
PSGC enrichment properties
Each feature carries:

psgc_id — stable entity URI
psgc_code — 10-digit Philippine Standard Geographic Code
psgc_name — canonical name
psgc_status — e.g. existing
match_confidence — exact | huc_map | fuzzy

title: Feature properties & schema
text:
Source NAMRIA attributes
The original NAMRIA shapefile attributes are preserved on each feature (e.g. ADM4_EN, ADM4_PCODE, ADM3_EN, …), so a feature can be joined back to either the PSGC or the NAMRIA identifier space.

title: Feature properties & schema
text:
Match confidence
The match_confidence field records how a feature’s PSGC code was resolved:

exact — direct PSGC code match
huc_map — resolved via the HUC mapping
fuzzy — matched by name similarity (lower confidence)

See HUC mapping for why HUCs need special handling, and coverage for per-level match statistics.

title: Special geographic areas & non-standard classes
text: This page documents the non-standard administrative classes shipped in the curated hierarchical output (2023-10-24/hierarchical_t0p005/). Beyond the standard per-class files (barangays, municipalities, cities, provinces, regions), the bundle also contains the files below.

title: Special geographic areas & non-standard classes
text:
Special Geographic Areas
Special Geographic Areas (SGAs) are nine units created under BARMM (Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao) legislation (the 2023 SGA Act) from barangays in North Cotabato that voted to join the BARMM. They sit outside the standard region → province → municipality → barangay hierarchy — they have no province or municipality parent — so they get their own class. Their PSGC codes share the 19999... prefix.

special_geographic_areas.geojson — the 9 SGAs (snapshot 2023-10-24).

curl -O https://github.com/bendlikeabamboo/barangay-boundaries-repository/releases/download/v2026.4.13.0/special_geographic_areas.geojson

text: The raw tier is the intermediate source stage of Pipeline B: NAMRIA shapefiles converted to GeoJSON by namria_converter.py, before any PSGC enrichment. It is kept in-repo for traceability — most users should use the curated hierarchical per-class files instead.

title: Raw pipeline stage (raw_t0p005/)
text:
What it is
adm0–adm4.geojson — the NAMRIA administrative-boundary shapefiles (v2023-11-06), converted to GeoJSON and simplified (Douglas-Peucker, default tolerance 0.005°). No PSGC properties are present yet; only the original NAMRIA attributes.






Note



Intermediate pipeline stage — most users want the curated hierarchical per-class files instead.

title: Raw pipeline stage (raw_t0p005/)
text:
File inventory
Kept in-repo at 2023-10-24/raw_t0p005/ for traceability:



File
Contents




adm0.geojson–adm4.geojson
NAMRIA boundaries (shapefile v2023-11-06) converted to GeoJSON and simplified; original NAMRIA attributes only, no PSGC properties yet


huc_adm2_mapping.json

The conversion runs Douglas-Peucker simplification at a default tolerance of 0.005° (hence the _t0p005 directory name). Full parameters are in Pipeline B.

title: Raw pipeline stage (raw_t0p005/)
text:

title: Download & versioning
text:
Release vs in-repo
Each PSGC snapshot is published two ways. Use whichever fits your workflow.








Path
What you get
When to use




GitHub Release (versioned)
Pinned hierarchical bundle + individual per-class files + manifest.json
Citing a specific snapshot, reproducible downloads, checksum verification


In-repo (always current)
The committed GeoJSON under 2023-10-24/{raw,enriched,hierarchical}_t0p005/, fetched via raw.githubusercontent.com
Pulling the latest tip of main, scripting against individual files, browsing source

title: Download & versioning
text:
Version tags
Every snapshot maps to a git tag of the form v<YYYY.M.DD.PATCH> (e.g. v2026.4.13.0). Pushing such a tag triggers the Release workflow, which builds and attaches the *-hierarchical.zip bundle, the individual per-class <class>.geojson files, and manifest.json to the matching GitHub Release:
git tag v2026.4.13.0
git push origin v2026.4.13.0
Release assets are version-pinned to that snapshot and never change. The in-repo files track main, so they reflect whatever is currently committed (typically the latest snapshot).
